transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I've got a cough, and it's causing a pain in the right side of my abdomen. It started two days ago.
When did you first notice it?
It started two days ago.
Is there anything that makes it better or worse?
The pain only comes on when I cough — that's what sets it off. Otherwise I haven't noticed anything that makes it better.
How would you describe the feeling in your own words?
The cough is a dry one — nothing comes up. The pain in my side just comes on sharp when I cough.
Where exactly do you feel it, and does it spread anywhere?
It's on the right side of my abdomen. I haven't noticed it spreading anywhere else.
On a scale from 0 to 10, where 10 is the worst, how bad is it?
I couldn't really put a number on it — it only bothers me when I cough, and otherwise it's not there.
Is it there all the time, or does it come and go?
It comes and goes — it's only there when I cough. Otherwise it's not bothering me at all.
Has anything else been bothering you along with this?
Yes, I've been feeling achy all over, and I've been feeling nauseous. I've also felt feverish with chills — my forehead felt warm at home.
Do you see a doctor regularly for any health condition?
Yes, I have high blood pressure and macular degeneration. I had pneumonia last year too, but that cleared up.
Which medicines do you take regularly, including any new ones?
I'm sorry, I can't remember the names of my medicines offhand.
Are you allergic to any medicines?
No, I'm not aware of any allergies.
Has this changed what you can do around the house or outside?
No, I haven't noticed any change in what I can do — I've been managing as usual.
Is there anything about this that worries you?
No, I can't say anything in particular is worrying me about it — I just thought I should get it checked.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
